intro: Follow a C source file through preprocessing, compilation, assembly, linking, and execution. Learn to recognise which stage failed rather than treating every failure as a syntax error.
outcomes: Identify headers, declarations, statements, and main.
Build and run a C11 program with warnings.
Distinguish translation, linking, runtime, and logic errors.
prerequisites: A terminal accepts commands. A file extension such as .c indicates source text. A library supplies reusable functions; a header tells the compiler about their interfaces.

sections.title: 1. Structure of a translation unit
paragraphs: A source file after preprocessing is a translation unit. Typical files contain preprocessing directives, declarations, and function definitions. There is no compulsory decorative division into documentation, link, and definition sections, though textbooks use those labels to organise examples.

The hosted entry forms include int main(void) and int main(int argc, char *argv[]). This unit uses the first. void main is not a portable hosted entry form. A return of zero reports successful termination; a nonzero result generally indicates failure to the calling environment.

A declaration introduces a name and type. A definition provides the object or function body. A function prototype describes parameter and return types so calls can be checked. Include the correct header before calling a library function.
example: The directive includes the stdio declarations. count is initialised before being read. printf receives a format string and an int matching %d. The observable output is Count: 3 followed by a newline.

sections.title: 2. Translation pipeline and commands
paragraphs: Preprocessing handles directives such as #include and macro substitution. Compilation checks and translates language constructs; assembly produces an object file. Linking combines object files and needed libraries into an executable. Toolchains can combine stages in one command.

With GCC installed, save the preceding example as hello.c. The first command builds it. The following commands illustrate inspecting preprocessing and producing an object without linking. These are alternatives, not extra steps required after a successful full build.

On PowerShell, run .\hello.exe for the Windows executable. On a Unix-like shell, a build named hello can be run as ./hello. Use the command appropriate to your installation; an online compiler may supply its own run button.
sections.code:
gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic hello.c -o hello
gcc -std=c11 -E hello.c -o hello.i
gcc -std=c11 -c hello.c -o hello.o

sections.title: 3. Diagnose by stage
paragraphs: A missing semicolon normally causes a translation diagnostic. A declared function called without a linked definition commonly causes an unresolved-symbol linking error. Reading invalid storage can cause a runtime failure, but undefined behaviour need not visibly crash. An incorrect average can be a logic error in an otherwise valid execution.

Warnings identify suspicious constructs but do not replace tests. Correct format strings, initialise values, and review conversion warnings. Sanitizers, where supported, help detect some invalid accesses and arithmetic errors; they are diagnostic aids, not a proof of safety.

A program may behave differently when optimised if it contains undefined behaviour. Do not fix that by merely disabling optimisation. Determine which language requirement was violated and correct the source.
example: If hello.c compiles but the shell says the executable cannot be found, check its output name, directory, and invocation syntax first. If linking fails for sqrt on a system requiring libm, add -lm after the source or object arguments. That is a toolchain library requirement, not a new C expression rule.

revision: Identify each part of the sample file.
Explain how an object differs from an executable.
Build with an explicit C standard and warnings.

questions.question: Is #include a function call?
answer: No. It is a preprocessing directive processed before ordinary compilation. It supplies header content, including declarations that let the compiler check library calls.

questions.question: A function is declared but its implementation is missing. Which stage commonly fails?
answer: The call can pass compilation because its declaration describes the interface. Linking commonly fails because the referenced function has no supplied definition. Include the correct object or library containing the implementation.

questions.question: Does a warning-free build prove there is no out-of-bounds access?
answer: No. Many bounds depend on runtime values the compiler cannot establish. Review index invariants and exercise boundary cases. Dynamic tools can detect particular failing executions but cannot prove correctness for all possible inputs.
